$comment: Branch protection for this repository, in the exact request shape of
PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection (#162).
Settings that live only in the GitHub UI are settings nobody can review,
diff, or restore. This file is the reviewable copy; scripts/check-branch-
protection.py checks it against docs/ci/REQUIRED-CHECKS.md on every PR, and
against the live API when given a token.
This file is not self-applying. Applying it needs admin scope:
scripts/check-branch-protection.py --apply develop   (prints the call)
The 15 checks that run on every PR regardless of base. CodeQL and the
container scan are excluded here because they do not run on a
develop-based PR at all — requiring a check that never reports leaves
the PR waiting on an `Expected` status forever.
Everything develop requires, plus the four checks that only run on a
main-based PR: CodeQL's three matrix legs and the container scan,
whose job `if:` tests github.base_ref == 'main'. On main they report,
so on main they are required.
enforce_admins is true here and not on develop: main is the published
branch, and an admin bypassing the gate set on it is the one case
where the audit trail matters more than the convenience.
Checks that run on PRs and are deliberately NOT required, each with the
reason. check-branch-protection.py fails when a PR check is in neither
this map nor a branch's contexts — so adding a gate to CI forces a
decision about whether it is part of the merge contract, rather than
letting it default to advisory by being forgotten.
Auto-merge is safe only once the contexts above are required: GitHub's
auto-merge waits for *required* checks, so arming it with none
configured merges immediately. That ordering is the whole reason #162
is blocked by #161 — the names have to exist and be stable first.
